headline: Pastrnak ruins Detroit's party while Celtics choke away a lead
morning_brew: Wednesday was a total rollercoaster that left me needing a second Dunks just to process it. The Bruins marched into Detroit and took care of business with a 4-1 win to absolutely trash their centennial celebration, which is exactly the kind of middle-finger-to-the-opposition hockey we needed after that pathetic home disaster earlier in the week. Jeremy Swayman was a brick wall with twenty-one saves, and watching David Pastrnak finally light the lamp along with Pavel Zacha and Casey Mittelstadt felt like the B's finally remembered how to play. The boys showed some real heart on the road, and I am praying this is the spark they need to actually show up when they return to the Garden this weekend.

Over on Causeway Street, it was a brutal night as the C's let a seventeen-point lead evaporate into a 105-101 loss to the Nuggets. We were playing with fire and eventually got scorched by Nikola Jokic and Jamal Murray, and frankly, it was a disaster. Jayson Tatum fought for his twenty-four points, but those six turnovers were back-breakers that made me want to throw my remote through the wall, and Neemias Queta's seventeen points were about the only bright spot in an otherwise dark night. Watching a lead like that vanish against a team like Denver is enough to drive a man to drink his coffee black, and I am honestly just ready for the weekend slate to get us back into the win column.

The Red Sox front office is already playing chess this winter, dragging in catcher Nick Fortes from the Rays to add some much-needed depth. It is a quiet time of year for baseball, but getting a guy behind the plate is a smart start to the offseason, unlike the Patriots, who have me looking at mock drafts and developing an early-season ulcer. We have a few days of calm before the B's and C's get back to action, so I am gonna use the time to let my blood pressure settle before I give myself a stroke.

trend_watch.trend: David Pastrnak dominated the ice with a goal and an assist in the four to one victory over the Red Wings.
trend_watch.dans_take: That is the kind of elite, game-changing performance I expect from him every single night.

trend_watch.trend: Jeremy Swayman shut the door on Detroit by stopping twenty-one of twenty-two shots for a stellar ninety-five percent save rate.
trend_watch.dans_take: He stood on his head when the defense let him down, and that is why we pay the man.

trend_watch.trend: Jayson Tatum struggled to protect the rock and finished the night with six turnovers in the narrow loss to Denver.
trend_watch.dans_take: You cannot throw the ball into the third row six times against a team like the Nuggets and expect a W.

news_digest.headline: Red Sox acquire catcher Nick Fortes in trade with Rays
news_digest.dans_take: A smart little move to patch a hole while the rest of the league is still napping.

news_digest.headline: Bruins beat Red Wings 4-1, spoil Detroit's Centennial celebration game
news_digest.dans_take: Nothing tastes better than a road win that ruins somebody else's big party.
